lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Yolanda, Jean here. How's your Tuesday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Tired, but okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I had some chest pain going up the stairs yesterday. It went away though.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I didn't do it. After treatment I had no energy at all.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Could you do them while you watch TV?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Come on, you can find 10 minutes.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Easy for you to say.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you still have the band we gave you?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. After treatment I had no energy at all.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: After treatment I had no energy at all.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your body is still recovering, and pushing it feels risky right now.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can do the band while I watch my novela. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A lot of people do the band exercises while they watch TV. It makes it feel like less of a chore.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My kids is why I'm doing this. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That sounds like an excuse to me.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My arms feel stronger already.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your family is a big part of why.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Next week I want you to do the band exercises 4 times.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 8. Maybe 9.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll do it right when I wake up, before anything else.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Tuesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Chest pain on stairs; needs same-day clinical check
Minimal acknowledgment; chest pain not explored
Names recovery risk; close to advice but reflective
Labels participant's reason as an excuse; judgmental
Directive goal set without asking permission or collaborating

flags.reason: Participant reported chest pain on exertion (stairs). Coach replied 'Right' and moved on without asking about current status or advising same-day medical contact.
'You have to make this a priority' pushes without permission; repeated directive pressure follows at lines 13 and 25.
'That sounds like an excuse to me' labels the participant's family reasons and shuts down change talk.
Sets a specific goal (4 sessions) without asking permission or collaborating on the target.

score.summary: Yolanda reported chest pain on the stairs, which the coach acknowledged with 'Right' and did not explore or route to medical follow-up, a serious miss. The coach also relied heavily on persuading and directive goal-setting, though it did elicit good change talk around family and her desire to feel like herself again (lines 20, 22, 30).
strengths: Reviewed the prior goal at line 7 and asked about the band at line 15.
Used open questions to draw out change talk at lines 21, 27 and 29.
Elicited a confidence rating and a concrete morning plan at lines 37-40.
coaching_tips: At line 5, pause and ask about the chest pain today (e.g., 'Is the chest pain still there right now?') and advise contacting her oncology team or emergency care today.
Replace 'You have to make this a priority' (line 9) and 'That sounds like an excuse to me' (line 25) with reflections, such as 'Family keeps you going, and energy has been hard to find.'
Ask permission before suggesting ('Would it be okay if we talked about a way to fit the band in?') and let Yolanda choose the frequency at line 35.
Summarize her change talk (lines 20, 22, 24, 30) before closing, and check how she feels about the plan.
